legend: A mandibular buccal bifurcation cyst overlies the buccal aspect of a mandibular second molar tooth. It appears as a well-demarcated, corticated radiolucency. Note that the periodontal space and lamina dura are intact and normal.
This paradental cyst is composed of an inflamed fibrous wall lined by hyperplastic epithelium. The cyst appears as an open pocket.
The epithelial lining is squamous and non-keratinized and shows secondary inflammatory changes with arcading rete hyperplasia and has no specific features.

This cyst appears as a well-demarcated and corticated radiolucency at the distobuccal aspect of an impacted third molar tooth. The follicular space surrounding the crown is intact and normal, seen as a narrow radiolucent rim around the crown posteriorly, excluding dentigerous cyst.

Paradental cyst is composed of an inflamed fibrous wall lined by proliferating epithelium, often showing an arcading pattern. The cyst is open at one aspect, where the lining may be continuous with the pericoronal or gingival tissues.
